scope: Same-host TCP. All native cells run five times; every sample retained. Diagnostic captures use separate short budgets and never enter timing results.
goal: portable pooled p50 <= min(current legacy,fixed C++), and positive reads/writes plus attempts <= C++ independently per process capture.
statistics: mean_ns is the pooled arithmetic mean; displayed ± run SD is sample SD (n-1) across five run means, not a confidence interval. Sample SD and extrema are retained separately.

head_commit.message:
Separate portable RPC runtime and bounded ownership

Break the portable API around explicit runtime, output, retained reader and
question ownership. Separate bounded queue admission from physical flush
completion and schedule output between buffered protocol turns.

Migrate maintained hosts and fixtures, verify ownership contracts and fault
controls, and record five-run native benchmarks with independent profiles
and IO traces. Keep the performance gap open: 8/24 latency cells qualify.

payload.evidence: Callback client Callgrind instructions 14594751 -> 14449821 (-0.993%); other profiled peers unchanged. Five-run native results are noisy, with an adverse unary-1k result retained.

burst8.decision: reject protocol burst; restore baseline scheduling
burst8.evidence: Five-run service-chain p50 regressed 36.5-64.9% against frozen portable in the same campaign, despite near-C++ or lower physical counts. All native and instrumented captures retained.

queue64.decision: Retain low-level construction and bounded-queue changes for measured instruction/startup-write savings; overall latency qualification fails and the gap stays open.
queue64.change: Keep baseline protocol/output scheduling; allow at most 64 outstanding owned transport frames rather than 32. Trace hypothesis: a 32-call burst plus Finish frames should not split at 32 receipts. Byte pool and admission credits unchanged.
queue64.evidence: Focused five-run service p50 within 2.7% of before; all three beat current legacy/C++. Fanout client socket writes 112 -> 111, wire writes 14 -> 13, matching C++ independently. Unary-1k Callgrind client/server instructions unchanged.
queue64.qualification: Full five-run matrix: 5/24 pooled-p50 passes versus 9/24 for frozen portable under the same references. Separate confirmation recovers several timing regressions but leaves dependent-read and callback slower. No general latency win claimed.

plan.reason: The full sweep showed pooled-p50 regressions in small calls and two topology cases despite mostly similar per-run modes. Focused and full timings disagree; instruction and IO evidence do not alone resolve native latency.
plan.decision: Run one additional five-repeat serial native confirmation after all qualification diagnostics, with the same four binaries, unchanged fixtures, warmups and sample counts. Retain the original full sweep as the qualification result.

validation.detail: 328 RPC and 151 allocating wire tests; 9 TCP/Unix transport integration tests with no default root features; 92 development-tool tests. The queue64 candidate received the RPC and transport checks; wire production source is unchanged from the earlier payload/burst8 tests.
Strict Clippy for RPC and wire on all targets, no-default-features wire compilation, alloc/unaligned/sync_reader wire compilation, and workspace formatting.

Five runs per cell, 480,000 native samples, 240 mixed implementation checks, unchanged fixtures and budgets, exact executable hashes, recomputed statistics, and separately captured socket/wire/profile evidence. All 48 original frame pairs and 304 directed topology edges match received frames.
Repository, wiki and workflow checks; source patch replays to the recorded source tree. All candidates and failed experiments are retained.

Corrected the stale reuse-before-finish-acceptance anchor without removing the owner guard or changing the expected failure. The development-tool suite checks all production mutation anchors. This fixes the observed parent CI failure before coverage.

validation.check: Full formal, Miri, coverage and independent C++ suites
validation.detail: No unsafe reader, engine ownership, or formal production model changes in this increment. Earlier qualification remains in the runtime-ownership report; it is not a fresh run for this candidate. Full coverage and independent C++ correctness remain separate from the affected tests and mixed benchmark checks.
